# Kungfu Kanban

> A local-first kanban board for Claude Code. You hand work out as cards from
> one Claude Code session. Each card runs as its own fresh session on the model
> it needs and comes back as a GitHub pull request, so your main session stays
> small and the backlog costs fewer tokens. Runs on your existing Claude
> subscription with no API keys. Free, MIT-licensed open source.

Key facts:

- The main session stays small. A bundled `kungfu-todo` skill lets any Claude
  Code session write cards and hand them to the board. The file reads, test
  output and retries happen inside each card's session. The session you are
  steering holds the plan, the card statuses and the PRs that come back.
- Every card is a fresh Claude Code session that starts with only its own
  prompt, so no session re-reads the history of earlier tasks.
- Model and effort are set per card (fable, opus, sonnet, haiku), so easy work
  runs on a cheap model.
- Follow-ups and CI fixes resume the card's own session. They do not start
  over.
- Runs entirely on your machine: one Express server, plain JSON files in
  `data/`; no accounts, no telemetry from the board app.
- Uses the Claude Code CLI with your subscription login; the runner strips
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment so it can never bill per token.
- Repo cards run in isolated git worktrees and open pull requests via the
  GitHub CLI, gated by CI; merged PRs file themselves into Done; conflicted
  PRs spawn self-healing fix agents.
- Cards can depend on each other ("runs after"): a dependent waits until its
  prerequisite is actually done, and an open, unmerged PR still counts as
  blocking. Cards can also share a group, which clusters them under one
  header, runs one card per group at a time, and sends a single
  group-complete notification.
- Subscription rate limits are absorbed: cards requeue, a countdown shows, and
  everything resumes when the window resets. Model-specific caps step launches
  down the fable → opus → sonnet → haiku ladder automatically.
- An optional LLM manager (the "Sensei") is off by default, because the Claude
  Code session driving the board does that job. Turned on, it triages cards,
  dispatches runs, reviews results against acceptance criteria and the actual
  PR diff, and can merge a PR once CI is green, with three autonomy levels
  (suggest / semi / auto).
- Phone access via token gate + Tailscale serve (tailnet-only), installable as
  a PWA, with ntfy push notifications.
- Import work from pasted markdown, dropped `.md` files, or open GitHub
  issues.
- Ships with the ponytail skill (vendored, MIT): agents default to the
  smallest working solution, which means less code and fewer output tokens per
  card. Auto-installed at boot and pre-selected on new cards.

## Docs

- [How the board saves tokens](https://github.com/LeahyCC/kungfu-kanban/blob/main/docs/token-savings.md):
  the mechanism, and the cases where a card is not worth it.
- [The manual](https://kungfu-kanban.com/#manual): complete setup and feature
  reference: requirements, install, PR flow, the Manager, phone access,
  limits, security.
- [Docs](https://kungfu-kanban.com/docs): linkable reference sections: the
  markdown import format, the Sensei's actions and autonomy levels,
  dependency/merge-gate semantics, and groups & lanes.
- [Compare](https://kungfu-kanban.com/compare): an honest comparison against
  Vibe Kanban, Conductor, and Crystal/Nimbalyst, the other tools people
  evaluate for running coding agents.
- [README](https://github.com/LeahyCC/kungfu-kanban#readme): the short
  version, with per-topic docs in
  [docs/](https://github.com/LeahyCC/kungfu-kanban/tree/main/docs).

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/LeahyCC/kungfu-kanban): MIT-licensed
  source code, issues, and releases.
